$comment: The one source of the look shared by the editor and the website. Edit here, then run `pnpm --filter @automata/editor tokens`; tokens.css is generated and both import it.

tokens: custom property name (without --) to its CSS value, verbatim. The website names come first (the field, paper, ink, cobalt, the chartreuse glow, the flutes and the curtain, the radii, the type steps); then what only the editor needs: a cobalt wash for selections, three state colours that read on paper, a pale red wash for what destroys, the scrim behind a dialog, two shadows (a raised control, a sheet), the layer and phase colours (projects store the layer names, so they keep theirs), spacing, the 44 and 48 px targets, and the fixed type ramp.
aliases: the editor's names from before the redesign, each the var() of a token, so code not yet moved to the token names takes the new look. They go once nothing reads them.

The editors' own look (the 2026-11-06 visual spec, after the taste skill's developer-tool scale): slightly rounded corners on one scale, --edge-sm 4px for controls and buttons, --edge-md 6px for panels, --edge-lg 8px for cards and dialogs, --edge-xl 12px for the top corners of a bottom sheet (the old --radius, --radius-sm, --radius-lg and --pill, 18, 12 and 26 px and a pill, are gone: the site and the editors share this one scale); flat paper controls instead of frosted glass; a flat chartreuse primary with an ink edge (--primary, --primary-ink, --primary-edge, --primary-hover) instead of the glow; shadows kept to a hairline lift. The website reads the same scale (its Examples and playground used the old radii until the 2026-11-07 fixes).
Where the two sets clashed, the website won: --font-sans and --font-mono are Geist.

The tool chrome (the Owner approved the redesign mockup on 2026-11-06): one neutral palette for every editor screen, --tool-bg the field, --tool-panel white panels, --tool-hover a row under the pointer, --tool-selected the chosen row, --tool-line and --tool-line-strong hairlines, --tool-muted and --tool-faint greys that read at 4.5:1 on white and on the chosen row, --tool-stage the near-black cabinet the level sits in. tool-chrome.css puts them under the names the kit reads, on the editor's pages only; the website keeps its field.

tokens.curtain: repeating-linear-gradient( 90deg, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2) 0, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.045) 46px, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2) 92px ), repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12) 0, transparent 70px, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12) 139px)
tokens.font-mono: "Geist Mono Variable", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
